sasha: repro for weird KV page-table growth on long contexts (H100 + A100). nightly canary OOM'd after ~22k tokens, mem steadily climbs ~200-300MB per 1k tokens. paging enabled. anyone seen this? @liam

liam: saw a blip in the canary logs last week but assumed config churn. which runtime commit and pager flags?

sasha: runtime: main@f2b3c9e, pager: enabled, page_size=65536, page_map_len=1024, kvmap=hybrid. repro script: `python tests/e2e/long_context_repro.py --model redwood/open-7b --seq 24000 --page-size 64k`
logs:
```
[2026-03-14T02:12:34Z] kv_pager: alloc_page -> idx=4294967295, page_map_len=1024
[2026-03-14T02:12:34Z] kv_pager: tagged_page->owner=0x7f8b1c, mapped_gpu=0
[2026-03-14T02:12:35Z] runtime: mem_total=45.2GB mem_used=50.1GB (OOM imminent)
```
looks like idx wraps to 2^32-1. repros reliably on H100 pool, sometimes on A100 but much less frequent.

adele: that idx value screams uint32_t wrap. we store page indexes in a 32-bit field anywhere in the kernel or PT metadata? differences across drivers/architectures could change allocation patterns so it only triggers on certain GPUs. do you have a pmap dump?

sasha: attached small pmap snippet (trimmed):
```
page_map_len=1024
entries: [0..1023] valid=~980 sparse=~44
observed alloc_index sequence: 1020, 1021, 1022, 1023, 0, 1, ... then suddenly -1(4294967295)
```
so it's not simple exhaustion, it's an arithmetic/overflow.

devon: quick hypothesis: we use a 32-bit counter in host-side pager state that gets incremented per allocation and occasionally pushed to device-side PT entry as `uint32_t`. On H100 the device kernel expects 64-bit or we read a 64-bit pointer back and cast/truncate incorrectly. Could also be wrap from using signed vs unsigned when decrementing free list.

liam: i can spin a debug build that makes index fields 64-bit and adds an assert when `idx >= page_map_len` before we write to PT on cpu side. if that catches it early we get a nicer repro. will test on dedicated H100 pool.

perf-bot: nightly-perf: h100-kvpager growth test: commit f2b3c9e -> mem_growth=4.9GB @22000 tokens; a100-kvpager growth test: mem_growth=1.1GB @22000 tokens. (quick metrics snapshot)

adele: good. also add guard in kernel path: if (idx >= page_map_len) return ERR_OVERFLOW; log full allocator state. otherwise device will happily index out of bounds into PT and corrupt neighboring metadata causing fragmentation and gradual growth.

sasha: stack trace when it OOMs shows multiple PT entries getting remapped instead of evicted -> reuse window shrinks. suspect corrupted free list pointers.

liam: patched locally: `kv/pagetable-index64` — changed pt_index type to uint64_t in host->device header and added assert. running canary now on h100 and a100. workaround for customers: set `page_size=131072` or cap `max_seq` to avoid hitting pathological allocator states.

devon: also check our atomic ops in the kernel that touch the page metadata. on Ampere vs Hopper the mem ops ordering might differ and expose race that shows up as weird index values. adding memory fence after free_list pop could help.

perf-bot: canary-run: h100 kvpager debug build: mem_growth=0.15GB @22000 tokens (initial). a100 debug run: mem_growth=0.18GB. commit test: kv/pagetable-index64 + perf assertions.

adele: if that looks stable let's: 1) land a small regression test in eng-runtime e2e/kv_pager/long_context (deterministic seed), 2) open GH issue referencing device logs and heapmap, 3) roll a canary to prod-dedicated for a day.

sasha: i'll open the issue and attach heapmap + driver logs. tagging @liam to own the PR. thanks all.

liam: assigned to me, pushing PR now. will add unit + e2e. :thumbsup:

sasha: nice, thanks. I'll monitor canary next 24h and post if anything odd pops up
